title: How much is left when three eighths go from five eighths?
description: A strip is cut into eight equal parts and five of them are shaded. Three shaded parts are taken away, and the answer is written in lowest terms.
teaching_notes: One idea: when two fractions count the same size of part, take away the top numbers, keep the bottom number, then write the answer in lowest terms. Watch for students who take away the bottom numbers too.

video_script.why: The child takes away fractions that count the same fractional unit by taking away parts of one strip, then writes the answer in lowest terms.
video_script.substitution: The same rectangular strip as the book's solved question about sevenths, now cut into eight equal parts.
video_script.anchor: a rectangular strip cut into eight equal parts with five parts shaded, as in the book
video_script.payoff_line: Five eighths take away three eighths is two eighths, which is one fourth

final_answer.spoken: two eighths, which is one fourth

video_script.fraction_reading: five eighths, three eighths, one eighth, two eighths, one fourth, four fifths, one fifth, three fifths
never_show: the remaining fraction before the answer beat
maths_rules: the strip is cut into 8 equal parts, so each part is 1/8; 5/8 is 5 shaded parts
5/8 and 3/8 count the same fractional unit 1/8, so the numerators are taken away: 5 − 3 = 2
check: 2 parts left + 3 parts taken away = 5 parts, which is 5/8
ground demo: 4/5 − 1/5 = 3/5 on a strip of 5 equal parts
video_script.design: One idea: same size of part, take away the tops, keep the bottom, then write in lowest terms. The strip stays on the board from start to end.

narration: <bookmark mark='demo'/>First look at a smaller strip, cut into five equal parts, with four parts shaded.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take away one shaded part, and three parts stay. Each part is still one fifth.
<bookmark mark='size'/>When the parts are the same size, we take away the number of parts and keep the size.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find five eighths take away three eighths.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: unit of 5/8 is 1/8; unit of 3/8 is 1/8; the units match

marks.same: the two units 1/8 are written side by side with a tick between them

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step one, check the size of the parts. We can only take away parts of the same size.
Both fractions count eighths, so the parts match.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: take away the tops and keep the bottom: (5 − 3)/8; 3 shaded parts slide off the strip

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step two, take away the tops and keep the bottom. This is the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Five parts take away three parts leaves two parts, and each part is still one eighth.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: lowest terms: 2 and 8 both divide by 2, so (2 ÷ 2)/(8 ÷ 2)

marks.low: the words lowest terms appear with 2 and 8 glowing
marks.half: (2 ÷ 2)/(8 ÷ 2) is written and the 8 parts group into pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step three, write the answer in lowest terms. Lowest terms means the top and the bottom share no factor except one.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Two and eight both divide by two, so divide the top and the bottom by two.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check: 2 parts left + 3 parts taken away = 5 parts of 1/8

marks.back: the 3 taken-away parts slide back beside the 2 parts that stayed

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, check by putting the answer back in the question.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Two parts left and three parts taken away make five parts, the five eighths we began with.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Five eighths take away three eighths is two eighths, which is one fourth.
